picks.headline: Stony Brook study finds viral BookTok bestseller Daggermouth is 60% AI-written
picks.excerpt: Using the AI-detection tool Pangram, Stony Brook University researchers found that roughly one in five randomly sampled Kindle ebooks contain substantial AI-generated text - and flagged #BookTok favorite Daggermouth by H.M. Wolfe as 60% AI-written. A concrete, method-driven look at how AI-generated fiction is slipping into bestseller lists and how detection now works.
picks.rationale: Net-new, URL- and content-distinct from every published books card (a different Book Riot article than the July book-banners and library round-up pieces). A method-driven detection study naming a BookTok bestseller as 60% AI-written is high-actionability for authors, publishers, and readers navigating AI fiction on the charts.

picks.headline: Publishing Perspectives launches a course to help publishers navigate the AI age responsibly
picks.excerpt: A four-week online course beginning January 2027 aims to give publishing professionals practical frameworks for implementing AI in editorial and production workflows and setting organizational policy. A signal of houses trying to operationalize AI in the craft rather than just debate it.
picks.rationale: Net-new and distinct from the other published Publishing Perspectives cards (Wiley/Genesis, the two 'Around the Book World' roundups). It shifts the AI-in-publishing story from litigation and debate toward operational, workflow-level frameworks editors and production teams can actually adopt. Given a distinct accent (#0070f3) since it shares the books category.
